statement: For any coin system containing a 1-unit coin, the greedy algorithm - repeatedly take the largest denomination not exceeding the remaining amount - uses the fewest coins possible.
definitions: Denominations are positive integers including 1; amounts are positive integers; 'fewest coins' = minimum number of coins (repetition allowed) summing exactly to the amount; greedy = repeatedly take the largest denomination not exceeding the remainder.
ground_truth_witness: Denominations {25, 10, 1} (US cents with no nickel), amount 40. Greedy takes 25, then 10, then five 1s: 7 coins. The optimum is four 10s: 4 coins. (Wikipedia gives the same phenomenon for the withdrawn Indian denominations {5,10,20,25} at 40 paise: greedy 25+10+5 = 3 coins, optimum 20+20 = 2 coins.)
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Claim precise (coin systems with a 1-coin; greedy = largest denomination first). Reference verified: {25,10,1} at 40 gives greedy 7 coins vs DP optimum 4 (Indian {5,10,20,25} at 40: 3 vs 2 also checks). Classic CLRS-exercise folklore; the solver must construct a system and an amount, but any of {1,3,4}@6 or {1,10,25}@30-40 works, so it is easy. No roster item concerns coin change.

bank_overlap.rationale: Greedy-is-not-optimal is a recurring bank theme (mse-232220-ans232981 ambulance dispatch, se-cs-16821-q greedy scheduling, se-cs-60677-a60690), but there is no change-making / coin-denomination entry (grep 'denomination', 'cents', 'nickel', 'make change' empty).
